title: Determination of gibberellic acid and abscisic acid in (Zea mays L.) (ICA-V305) seeds germinated using dynamic sonication assisted solvent extraction and maceration
author: Rivera, Ocampo-Serna, et al.

steps.title: Prepare extraction solvent
steps.instruction: Mix methanol with formic acid to obtain a 5.0 % (v/v) formic acid solution in an 80:20 methanol‑formic acid ratio; this solvent will be used for all extractions.

steps.title: Dynamic DSASE extraction (continuous flow)
steps.instruction: Extract 1.0000 ± 0.0005 g of powdered maize seed in a stainless‑steel ultrasound cell using continuous solvent flow.

substeps.instruction: Weigh 1.0000 ± 0.0005 g of seed powder and place it in a stainless‑steel extraction cell.
Insert the cell into a Branson 5210 ultrasound bath (output power 130 W, frequency 40 kHz) and maintain the bath temperature between 20 °C and 35 °C.
Connect a peristaltic pump to the cell and set the solvent flow to 0.5 mL min⁻¹.
Run the extraction for 20.0 min (continuous flow).
Collect the extract, concentrate it in a rotary evaporator at 35.0 °C, and store the concentrate at 4.0 °C until HPLC analysis.

steps.title: Static DSASE extraction (flow pause)
steps.instruction: Extract 1.0000 ± 0.0005 g of seed powder with a solvent flow that is stopped for a defined interval.

substeps.instruction: Weigh 1.0000 ± 0.0005 g of seed powder and place it in a stainless‑steel extraction cell.
Place the cell in the same Branson 5210 ultrasound bath (130 W, 40 kHz) and keep the temperature at 20–35 °C.
Connect the peristaltic pump and set the flow to 0.5 mL min⁻¹.
Run solvent flow for 10.0 min, stop the flow for 5.0 min, then resume flow for another 10.0 min (total 25 min).
Collect the extract, concentrate it at 35.0 °C in a rotary evaporator, and store at 4.0 °C until HPLC analysis.

steps.title: Maceration extraction
steps.instruction: Perform three successive macerations of 1.0000 ± 0.0005 g seed powder with methanol‑formic acid solvent.

substeps.instruction: Weigh 1.0000 ± 0.0005 g of seed powder and place it in a glass vial.
Add 5.0 mL of the methanol‑formic acid 5.0 % (80:20) solvent.
Shake the vial for 1.0 h at room temperature (20.0 °C).
Decant the supernatant into a clean vial.
Add another 5.0 mL of solvent to the remaining pellet and repeat the shaking for 1.0 h; collect the supernatant.
Repeat the addition, shaking, and decanting a third time (total three extracts).
Combine all three supernatants, then centrifuge the combined extract at 7000 rpm for 20.0 min.
Concentrate the centrifuged extract at 35.0 °C in a rotary evaporator and store the concentrate at 4.0 °C until HPLC analysis.

steps.title: Concentrate extracts and store
steps.instruction: Remove solvent from all extracts and keep them refrigerated before analysis.

substeps.instruction: Use a rotary evaporator set to 35.0 °C to evaporate the solvent from each extract (DSASE‑D, DSASE‑S, and maceration).
Transfer the dried residues to labeled vials and store them at 4.0 °C until HPLC injection.

steps.title: Filter extracts before HPLC
steps.instruction: Clarify each concentrated extract by filtration.

substeps.instruction: Pass each stored extract through a 0.2 µm pore PVDF membrane filter into HPLC‑compatible vials.

steps.title: Set up HPLC and run samples
steps.instruction: Analyze filtered extracts by HPLC under the specified chromatographic conditions.

substeps.instruction: Install a Supelcosil LC‑18‑DB column (150 × 4.6 nm, 5.0 µm) on a Shimadzu HPLC equipped with a degasser (DGU‑205), diode‑array detector (SPD‑M20A), oven (CTO‑10AS VP), and autosampler (SIL‑10AF).
Prepare mobile phase A (acetonitrile) and mobile phase B (0.01 % formic acid).
Set the flow rate to 0.5 mL min⁻¹.
Program a linear gradient: 0–5 min 10 % A / 90 % B, 5–45 min 70 % A / 30 % B, 45–55 min 10 % A / 90 % B (total run 55 min).
Inject 10 µL of each filtered extract using the autosampler.
Detect gibberellic acid (GA₃) and abscisic acid (ABA) at 195 nm.
Perform each injection in triplicate and record the mean peak area ± standard deviation.

steps.title: Perform calibration and statistical analysis
steps.instruction: Generate calibration curves and evaluate data quality using linear regression and ANOVA.

substeps.instruction: Prepare standard solutions of GA₃ and ABA (e.g., 2.0 mg kg⁻¹ GA₃ and 0.2 mg kg⁻¹ ABA) and inject them under the same HPLC conditions to obtain peak areas.
Fit a simple linear regression (ordinary least squares) of peak area versus concentration for each hormone.
Record regression parameters: GA₃ intercept β₀ = 0.267 (SD = 0.402), slope β₁ = 1.607 (SD = 0.230), R² = 0.99; ABA intercept β₀ = 0.232 (SD = 0.381), slope β₁ = 1.273 (SD = 0.416), R² = 0.97.
Verify that the regression model meets the assumptions of normality, homoscedasticity, and independence.

Analyze the experimental data with one‑way ANOVA (α = 0.05, 95 % confidence interval) to test for significant differences among extraction methods; report p‑values (e.g., p = 0.0001 for ABA, p = 0.0662 for GA₃).
